questions.q: Where should `raw_orders` be declared before a staging model reads it?
options: It doesn't need to be declared anywhere
Hard-coded as a table name directly inside the staging model's SQL
In `sources.yml`, as a table under the jaffle_shop source
In the Power BI connection dialog
questions.explain: Like raw_customers, raw_orders is declared once in sources.yml so models reference it by name via source(), not a hard-coded identifier.

options: `order_date` to `date`, and `status` to `state`
`id` to `order_id`, and `user_id` to `customer_id`
No renames — the model selects raw columns unchanged
`id` to `pk`, and `status` to `order_status`
questions.explain: id becomes order_id (the project's <entity>_id convention) and user_id becomes customer_id so it joins cleanly to the customers mart.

options: Because `user_id` is not a valid SQL identifier
So this model joins cleanly to the customers mart on a matching column name in Lesson 4
Because dbt requires every foreign key to be named `customer_id`
It's purely cosmetic and has no downstream effect
questions.explain: The rename sets up the exact join Lesson 4 performs between this staging model and the customers mart.

questions.q: What should a staging model NOT contain, by convention?
options: A reference to `{{ source(...) }}`
Any `select` statement
Joins to other sources or business logic
Column renames
questions.explain: A staging model's job is narrow: read one source, rename columns, nothing else — no joins, no business logic.

questions.q: How should you confirm `stg_jaffle_shop__orders` built correctly?
options: Open Power BI and check if a report renders
Assume it's correct if `dbt run` doesn't print an error
There's no way to confirm it before Lesson 4
Query it directly in Snowflake and confirm order_id/customer_id are populated and status values match what was recorded from raw_orders
questions.explain: Querying the built model directly and comparing against the known raw data is how you confirm, rather than assume, it's correct.
